Design function: Manufacturable TCAN4550 RGY0020A land pattern
Potential failure mode: Incorrect perimeter-pad centers cause solder bridging or opens
Potential effect: Low yield or nonfunctional CAN controller
Cause or mechanism: Prior custom footprint interpreted pad-center dimensions incorrectly
Current controls: Corrected pad and stencil centers against TI 4225320/A; copies hash-match
Recommended action: Independent overlay review; PCB DRC; first-article AOI/X-ray inspection
Closure evidence: Accepted footprint overlay; clean DRC; accepted first-article solder inspection

Design function: Safe MCU wake across CAN and MCU power domains
Potential failure mode: nWKRQ default 3.6 V reaches MCU while MCU VDDS is low or absent
Potential effect: Absolute-maximum violation; back-powering; excess sleep current; latch-up or damage; false or missed wake
Cause or mechanism: Mixed power domains; default internal 3.6 V output exists before SPI configuration; direct connection and R307 100k pull-up lack power-off isolation
Current controls: Schematic warning; firmware bit 19 requirement; datasheet review
Recommended action: Add automotive over-voltage-tolerant buffer with Ioff/partial-power-down protection (for example SN74LVC1G17-Q1); define TCAN-off state; remove or reassign raw pull-up; configure and read back bits 19 and 8
Closure evidence: Approved schematic and ERC; all VSUP/VIO/reset/sleep sequences tested; MCU pin within limits; no back-power current

Design function: Maintain input filter damping across service life
Potential failure mode: C101 ESR rise and capacitance loss; eventual open circuit
Potential effect: Under-damped input filter; buck instability; raised conducted emissions; loss of hot-plug surge absorption
Cause or mechanism: Panasonic EEEFK2A220P is an FK-series 105 degC / 2000 h wet electrolytic on an always-on rail - roughly one year continuous at high ambient. It is the only wet electrolytic on the board and its AEC-Q200 status is claimed in the schematic note but NOT confirmed against the datasheet
Current controls: R101 1 ohm series damping partner; 100 V part on a 36 V maximum rail gives large voltage derating
Recommended action: Confirm AEC-Q200 status from the Panasonic datasheet; compute required life at the target ambient; if 2000 h is insufficient move to an automotive hybrid-polymer part or an all-ceramic bank - and re-check input filter damping if the electrolytic is removed
Closure evidence: Life calculation at target ambient plus the selected part datasheet and a damping re-check

Design function: Stable 40 MHz reference clock
Potential failure mode: Crystal fails to start or stop; excessive drive/amplitude; excessive frequency error
Potential effect: No or intermittent CAN; CAN-FD bit errors; temperature-dependent field failure; reduced crystal life
Cause or mechanism: Unmeasured PCB stray capacitance and loop margin; R311 0 ohm is provisional; component and layout variation; CAN_XTAL2 trace is 8.78 mm against CAN_XTAL1 at 3.23 mm so the loop is asymmetric
Current controls: 40 MHz CL8 crystal; C303/C304 10 pF C0G; R311 tuning footprint at OSC1; TI SLLA549 note
Recommended action: Characterize EVT hardware across voltage and temperature; tune R311/C303/C304; confirm frequency and drive level against the exact ordered crystal limit
Closure evidence: Signed oscillator test report with equipment/probe loading/board revision/sample count/corners/final BOM values
Status: OPEN - close after EVT before production fabrication

Design function: Manufacturable CAN common-mode choke
Potential failure mode: L301 land pattern or terminal numbering does not match the specified TDK ACT45B
Potential effect: Open or swapped windings - CAN non-functional or with no common-mode filtering; scrapped first article
Cause or mechanism: L301 is assigned the generic Inductor_SMD:L_CommonModeChoke_Coilank_ACM4532 pattern (4.5 x 3.2 mm) rather than a pattern derived from the TDK drawing. Symbol variant _1423 was selected so windings pair 1-4 and 2-3 to match that footprint layout (pads 1 and 2 one side; 3 and 4 the other)
Current controls: Requirement recorded in the component Purpose field; BOM open item OA-2; ARCHITECTURE.md note. Netlist verified as CAN_P to pin 1; CAN_BUS_P to pin 4; CAN_N to pin 2; CAN_BUS_N to pin 3
Recommended action: Obtain the TDK ACT45B land-pattern drawing; verify pad geometry AND terminal numbering; if ACT45B pairs its windings differently swap the symbol variant and re-verify the netlist; independent overlay review before release
Closure evidence: Footprint overlay against the manufacturer drawing plus a winding continuity check on the first article

Design function: Maintain connections under vehicle vibration
Potential failure mode: J101 or J301 screw terminals loosen; J401 or J201 unmate
Potential effect: Intermittent power or CAN or total loss of function; intermittent faults are very hard to diagnose in the field
Cause or mechanism: None of the four external connectors has a vibration rating. Phoenix MPT screw terminals rely on screw torque alone; JST PH uses friction retention; U.FL has no lock and is rated for roughly 30 mating cycles
Current controls: Four M2 mounting holes H1-H4 with grounded pads secure the board itself to the enclosure
Recommended action: Replace all external connectors with sealed locking automotive types for production (alternatives listed in the BOM); specify screw torque and thread-locking for any prototype field trial; consider a U.FL retainer or a soldered antenna pigtail
Closure evidence: Production connector selection record plus vibration testing to the target ISO 16750-3 profile
Status: OPEN - prototype-grade by explicit design decision

Design function: Reliable exposed-pad solder and thermal joint
Potential failure mode: Voiding; insufficient solder; solder wicking into thermal vias under U101 U102 U201 U301
Potential effect: Degraded heat sinking which raises the THM-001 risk; unstable ground reference; intermittent or nonfunctional devices
Cause or mechanism: Four exposed-pad packages carry thermal via-in-pad arrays (U101 10 vias; U201 10; U102 6; U301 6). Vias in pad wick solder unless plugged and capped. Tenting is requested on both faces but via plugging or filling is NOT specified in the fabrication notes
Current controls: Paste apertures defined in the supplied stencil layers; CAN-003 already corrected the U301 land pattern against TI drawing 4225320/A
Recommended action: Decide and specify via-in-pad treatment (plugged and capped versus tented only) in FAB_NOTES.md; agree stencil aperture design with the assembler; X-ray first articles against IPC-A-610 class 2 void limits
Closure evidence: X-ray images of all four devices on the first article plus an agreed stencil drawing

Design function: Survive handling ESD during assembly programming and service
Potential failure mode: ESD damage at J202 J201 J401 or the bare test points
Potential effect: Latent or immediate MCU or RF damage; field failures with no clear root cause
Cause or mechanism: J202 Tag-Connect exposes SWDIO SWDCK and RESET directly to MCU pins with no series protection; J201 U.FL connects to the RF port through the matching network; TP101-TP103 and TP401-TP403 are bare pads. Only the CC2340R53 device-level pin ESD rating protects these nodes
Current controls: No specific circuit protection - relies on device ESD ratings and factory ESD control
Recommended action: Require ESD-controlled handling in the assembly and service work instructions; if field programming is expected add series resistors or a low-capacitance ESD array on the SWD lines
Closure evidence: ESD handling procedure in the released work instruction plus a decision record on SWD protection

Design function: Maintain creepage and clearance on the 9-36 V input section
Potential failure mode: Board is built or field-serviced without conformal coating
Potential effect: Dendrite growth or arcing between the VIN nets and GND under humidity and contamination; field short across the vehicle supply
Cause or mechanism: All netclasses use 0.2 mm clearance including the 9-36 V nets. A DRC run against an IPC-2221 Table 6-1 row B2 rule (external uncoated 31-50 V requires 0.6 mm) returned 118 clearance violations with a minimum actual spacing of 0.2005 mm. The design is compliant only under row B4 (external with permanent polymer coating requires 0.13 mm)
Current controls: Coating declared MANDATORY in hardware/Manufacturing_Output_Files/FAB_NOTES.md with a masking list; recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md assumptions
Recommended action: Make conformal coating a line item on the assembly drawing and the purchase order rather than only a note; add an incoming-inspection check; consider widening the local pour clearance around J101 and F101 to 0.6 mm so the uncoated case is also safe
Closure evidence: Assembly drawing revision and a signed process sheet showing coating and masking

Design function: Deliver rated BLE output power and receive sensitivity
Potential failure mode: Antenna matching network does not present the intended impedance to the MCU RF port
Potential effect: Reduced TX power and RX sensitivity - direct BLE range loss; possible variance against regulatory power limits
Cause or mechanism: Measured from the layout: the U201 ANT pad sits at x = 132.0 mm and the first matching element C214/L202 at x = 138.29 mm so 6.29 mm of line precedes the match. At 2.44 GHz on this stackup (eeff about 3.2; guided wavelength about 69 mm) that is roughly 33 degrees of electrical length which rotates the source impedance. L202 2.8 nH and C214/C216 1.5 pF were taken from the TI LP-EM-CC2340R53 reference where those parts sit immediately at the pin
Current controls: Values are datasheet-derived; TDK DLF162500LT low-pass filter follows the match; continuous In1 ground reference at 0.11 mm
Recommended action: Either relocate the matching network adjacent to the ANT pad or re-tune L202/C214/C216 on a VNA for the as-built geometry including the LPF and U.FL; measure conducted TX power and sensitivity; add DNP tuning placeholders for future adjustment
Closure evidence: VNA S11 plot at the U.FL port plus conducted power and sensitivity measurements

Design function: Radiate at the intended pattern and efficiency
Potential failure mode: Antenna detuning or blockage by the enclosure metal or mounting position
Potential effect: Severe BLE range loss in the installed position regardless of board-level RF performance
Cause or mechanism: The design terminates at a U.FL port. No antenna part is selected and no enclosure or mounting position is defined. Metal proximity cable routing and ground-plane coupling all remain open
Current controls: U.FL allows the antenna to be positioned away from the board; board ground is continuous across In1 and B.Cu
Recommended action: Select the antenna and pigtail; define mounting position and keepout relative to metal; measure total radiated power and efficiency in the final enclosure
Closure evidence: Radiated performance measurement in the intended installation
Status: OPEN - antenna and enclosure selection required before production

Design function: Define battery charge management responsibility
Potential failure mode: Pack discharged below its safe floor or charged by an unsuitable external source
Potential effect: Cell damage and capacity loss; in the worst case a lithium-ion safety event
Cause or mechanism: Deliberate architecture decision (see README.md design decisions and ARCHITECTURE.md) - there is no charger on this board and protection is delegated entirely to the pack PCM. The board can neither recharge nor monitor the pack
Current controls: J401 specified for a protected 1S pack of 3.0 to 4.2 V; U402 draws only 2.8 uA so board drain is low; VBAT_SENSE divider is provisioned
Recommended action: Specify required pack PCM parameters (over-discharge cutoff over-current and short-circuit) as a controlled purchased-part requirement; document the external charging procedure; connect VBAT_SENSE per BAT-005 so firmware can at least warn
Closure evidence: Approved pack specification document plus a firmware low-battery behaviour test
Status: OPEN - assumption that a protected pack is always fitted

Design function: Survive vehicle transients on the 9-36 V input
Potential failure mode: Transient above the D101 standoff propagates to the buck input
Potential effect: Buck damage and loss of all rails; cascade loss of CAN and BLE
Cause or mechanism: D101 SM8S40CA has a 40 V reverse standoff with only 4 V margin over the 36 V maximum input and a specified maximum clamping voltage of 64.5 V at 102 A on a 10/1000 us pulse. Repetitive or longer-duration ISO 7637-2 pulse energy has not been characterised
Current controls: F101 T1A fuse; D101 8000 W bidirectional TVS; R101 1 ohm series damping; U101 LMR38010-Q1 rated 80 V recommended and 85 V absolute maximum so the 64.5 V clamp sits inside the device rating
Recommended action: Run ISO 7637-2 pulses 1 2a 3a 3b and 5a and the ISO 16750-2 load dump case against assembled hardware; verify TVS clamp energy and fuse coordination; re-check the 40 V standoff against 36 V plus supply tolerance
Closure evidence: Transient test report with generator settings sample count and pass/fail per pulse

Design function: Establish and maintain correct CAN controller configuration
Potential failure mode: Firmware fails to re-apply register configuration after a device reset or undervoltage recovery
Potential effect: nWKRQ left in its unsafe default 3.6 V mode per CAN-001; incorrect wake behaviour; M_CAN unconfigured so no CAN traffic passes
Cause or mechanism: The TCAN4550 digital core resets and loses M_CAN configuration on a UVIO or UVSUP protected-mode event. A vehicle crank dip can trigger exactly this because UVSUP falling is specified at 4.5 to 4.7 V. The MCU also drives RST from DIO10 with R305 as a pull-down and the pin is active HIGH
Current controls: R305 pull-down keeps the device out of reset while the MCU is tri-stated; requirement recorded in schematic notes and in CAN-001
Recommended action: Firmware shall set register 0x0800 bit 19 to select nWKRQ VIO open-drain mode before any sleep; read back all configuration after every reset; re-initialise M_CAN after any UVSUP recovery; add an automated power-cycle soak test
Closure evidence: Firmware review plus an automated power-cycle test demonstrating correct re-initialisation over many cycles

Design function: Start and hold the 48 MHz high-frequency oscillator
Potential failure mode: HFXT fails to start or frequency error exceeds the BLE requirement
Potential effect: No BLE operation at all or link failure and range loss from frequency offset
Cause or mechanism: C210 and C211 are DNP so the design relies on the CC2340R5 internal load-capacitance array to reach the ABM11W 7 pF CL. Measured from the layout the X48P trace is 11.07 mm and X48N 7.63 mm - long and asymmetric by 3.4 mm - adding uncharacterised stray capacitance. X202 also sits only about 2.5 mm from L202 in the RF matching network
Current controls: C210/C211 footprints retained as a fallback; crystal selected as a TI-compatible 7 pF part
Recommended action: Measure startup time frequency error and drive level across temperature on assembled hardware; if the internal array cannot reach CL then fit C210/C211; shorten and balance the X48P and X48N traces in the next layout revision
Closure evidence: Oscillator characterisation report across supply and temperature corners

Design function: Meet vehicle radiated and conducted emissions limits on the CAN port
Potential failure mode: Common-mode noise couples from the node onto the vehicle harness
Potential effect: CISPR 25 radiated emissions failure and rejection at vehicle level
Cause or mechanism: CAN_P and CAN_N are length-matched to 15.58 mm each but their edge-to-edge spacing varies from roughly 0.4 mm to 2.8 mm along the run so coupling and differential impedance are not controlled. The split termination which the TCAN4550 datasheet describes as providing common-mode filtering is DNP
Current controls: L301 ACT45B common-mode choke fitted at the transceiver per TCAN4550 datasheet section 11.1; D301 at the connector; solid In1 ground plane under the pair; U101 is the spread-spectrum buck variant
Recommended action: Re-route CAN_P and CAN_N as a uniformly coupled pair using the now-corrected CAN netclass (0.2 mm gap 0.17 mm width); run an EMC pre-scan before formal CISPR 25 testing
Closure evidence: Updated layout showing constant pair spacing plus a pre-scan plot

Design function: Prevent cross-connection of the power and CAN harnesses
Potential failure mode: CAN harness landed on J101 or vehicle power landed on J301
Potential effect: 9-36 V applied directly to the CAN bus pins - immediate destruction of U301 and possible damage to every other node on the bus
Cause or mechanism: J101 and J301 are both Phoenix MPT 2.54 mm terminal blocks from the same family differing only in pole count (2 versus 3)
Current controls: Different pole counts make direct cross-mating of a pre-made harness physically impossible and the silkscreen labels each section. However these are screw terminals so individual wires can still be landed in the wrong block
Recommended action: Move to keyed non-interchangeable connectors for production as listed in the BOM alternatives; in the meantime add explicit per-terminal silkscreen labelling and a wiring diagram in the bring-up procedure
Closure evidence: Production connector selection record plus a bring-up wiring diagram
Status: OPEN - prototype connectors accepted; production change required

Design function: Keep parked current inside the vehicle quiescent budget
Potential failure mode: Module draws more standby current than the vehicle allows
Potential effect: Vehicle battery discharge during extended parking; warranty complaint
Cause or mechanism: The R102 383k and R103 100k enable divider draws about 25 uA at 12 V and 50 uA at 24 V continuously and cannot be switched off. Adding LMR38010-Q1 at 40 uA TPS7B81-Q1 at 2.7 uA plus TCAN4550 sleep and MCU standby gives an estimated 100 to 150 uA total. This is datasheet arithmetic and has never been measured
Current controls: PFM and low-Iq parts selected deliberately for this purpose; TCAN4550 INH is left unconnected so no rail gating currently exists
Recommended action: Measure actual parked current at 12 V and 24 V in the deepest sleep state and compare against the OEM budget; if over budget use the TCAN4550 INH output to gate the buck enable instead of the fixed divider
Closure evidence: Measured current log at both supply voltages with the firmware sleep state recorded

Design function: Allow firmware to report pack state and the active power source
Potential failure mode: Firmware cannot read battery voltage or determine which source is active
Potential effect: No low-battery warning; no source reporting; no graceful shutdown - field pack failures are silent
Cause or mechanism: VBAT_SENSE (R403 R404 C404) and USING_BATTERY_N (R405 and the U404 ST pin) terminate at unconnected global labels. ERC flags both as single-instance labels. Sixteen CC2340 GPIOs including every ADC-capable channel are free
Current controls: Divider and pull-up are fitted and electrically correct - only the MCU connection is missing. The gap is documented in ARCHITECTURE.md
Recommended action: Route VBAT_SENSE to an ADC-capable DIO such as DIO7_A0 and USING_BATTERY_N to a spare GPIO; re-run ERC; add firmware battery and source reporting
Closure evidence: Updated schematic with clean ERC plus firmware correctly reading both signals
Status: OPEN - known functional gap and cheap to fix

Design function: Keep TCAN4550 I/O within specification in every power state
Potential failure mode: VIO sits at about 3.0 V which is below the 3.135 V recommended minimum
Potential effect: Digital I/O levels are not guaranteed; undefined SPI behaviour if firmware accesses the device during backup
Cause or mechanism: In battery backup +3V3_SYS equals +3V0_BAT minus the LM66100 conduction drop so VIO remains powered at about 3.0 V while VSUP is absent. This sits above the 2.45 to 2.6 V UVIO rising threshold so the device does not enter protected mode - it simply operates outside its recommended window
Current controls: ACCEPTED BY DESIGN - CAN is defined as unavailable in backup and VSUP is absent anyway. The alternative of powering VIO from the vehicle rail only was rejected because it creates the powered-MCU and unpowered-VIO partial-power-down condition that is the CAN-001 mechanism
Recommended action: Firmware shall not initiate SPI transactions while USING_BATTERY_N indicates backup - this requires BAT-005 to be closed first; confirm there is no elevated leakage into VIO at 3.0 V
Closure evidence: Firmware state-machine review plus a leakage measurement taken in backup mode
Status: OPEN - accepted out-of-specification condition and documented

Design function: Prevent incorrect battery connection
Potential failure mode: Pack pigtail inserted reversed or a non-conforming pack connected
Potential effect: Damage to U401 and U402; pack short; potential lithium-ion thermal event
Cause or mechanism: J401 is a polarised JST PH which prevents reversed insertion of a correctly wired pigtail but does not prevent a mis-wired pigtail or a pack outside the assumed 3.0 to 4.2 V range
Current controls: Polarised connector; U401 reverse-current blocking; F401 1 A fuse; polarity to be marked on the silkscreen
Recommended action: Confirm BAT+ and BAT- polarity marking is present and legible next to J401; specify the pack pigtail wiring as a controlled purchased item; add a first-use polarity check to the bring-up procedure
Closure evidence: Silkscreen inspection on the first article plus an approved pack pigtail drawing

Design function: Release a buildable bill of materials
Potential failure mode: Eight line items carry no manufacturer part number
Potential effect: Assembler substitutes parts; RF match and MCU DC/DC behaviour change unpredictably between builds
Cause or mechanism: L201 L202 C201-C204/C206/C207/C215 C205/C208 C209 C214/C216 and R201 were placed by value only. L202 and C214/C216 are RF-critical and L201 must meet the TI saturation-current and DCR requirement for the CC2340R5 internal DC/DC
Current controls: Values packages and footprints are all defined; candidate parts and the RF-grade requirement are recorded in BOM_NOTES.md open item OA-3
Recommended action: Assign AEC-Q200 parts for all eight line items using RF-grade high-Q parts for L202 and C214/C216 and a TI-compatible inductor for L201
Closure evidence: Released BOM carrying committed manufacturer part numbers

Design function: Ride through engine crank without resetting the BLE application
Potential failure mode: Buck disables during crank or oscillates around the enable threshold
Potential effect: BLE link drop and loss of session; repeated MCU reset; poor user experience during every start
Cause or mechanism: The R102 383k and R103 100k divider gives a ratio of 4.83. With the LMR38010-Q1 enable thresholds specified as 1.1 to 1.4 V rising and 0.95 to 1.22 V falling the turn-on point spans 5.31 to 6.76 V and turn-off spans 4.59 to 5.89 V across tolerance - a wide band that has not been measured on hardware
Current controls: Divider sized for roughly 6.0 V nominal turn-on which is deliberately below the 9 V specification minimum to extend crank ride-through; U403/U404 ORing hands the MCU domain over to the 3.0 V battery rail below that point
Recommended action: Sweep the input from 4 to 9 V on the bench at full load and record the exact turn-on and turn-off points; confirm clean ORing handover with no rail collapse or threshold chatter
Closure evidence: Supply sweep plot showing +6V5_CAN +3V3_VEH +3V3_SYS and the MCU reset state

Design function: Provide the 32.768 kHz low-frequency sleep clock
Potential failure mode: LSE fails to start or carries excessive frequency error
Potential effect: BLE connection timing drift; higher current from widened receive windows; dropped connections
Cause or mechanism: C212 and C213 at 15 pF assume roughly 1.5 pF of board stray against the ABS06 9 pF CL and that stray was never measured. The crystal is also rated only to +85 degC while the surrounding automotive ICs are rated to +125 degC and it is a commercial non-AEC-Q200 part
Current controls: Traces are short at X32P 4.92 mm and X32N 3.83 mm; ESR specified at 90 kohm maximum
Recommended action: Measure LSE startup and frequency error across the target temperature range; select an AEC-Q200 32.768 kHz crystal for production and re-check the load capacitance
Closure evidence: LSE characterisation report across the target temperature range

Design function: Minimise pack drain when the vehicle supply is absent
Potential failure mode: Backup pack discharges faster than the runtime estimate
Potential effect: No BLE availability when it is actually needed; deep-discharge damage to the cell
Cause or mechanism: Continuous drain is U402 at 2.8 uA plus the R403/R404 1 Mohm divider at 2.1 uA plus LM66100 leakage giving roughly 6 to 8 uA before any BLE activity. The 2 Mohm divider alone accounts for about 17 mAh per year. These are datasheet figures and have never been measured
Current controls: Low-Iq parts chosen deliberately throughout the backup branch; 1 Mohm divider values keep sense drain low
Recommended action: Measure actual pack drain with the vehicle rail absent for both BLE idle and advertising states; compute realistic runtime for the selected pack capacity
Closure evidence: Measured drain figures plus a runtime calculation for the specified pack

Design function: Correct bus termination for the installed network topology
Potential failure mode: Module fitted as a bus end node without termination or as a stub with termination fitted
Potential effect: Signal reflections and bit errors; degraded or failed CAN FD at higher data rates
Cause or mechanism: R302 and R303 at 60.4 ohm and C309 at 4.7 nF are DNP. The design ASSUMES the module is a stub node because no network topology was specified
Current controls: Split-termination footprints provided with the centre tap returned to GND through C309; DNP intent documented on the schematic and carried into the BOM
Recommended action: Obtain the actual network topology from the vehicle integrator; record the fitted or not-fitted decision in a build variant document; if an end node fit all three parts together for 120.8 ohm
Closure evidence: Written topology confirmation from the integrator plus a build-variant BOM

Design function: Survive handling and in-vehicle ESD at the exposed CAN bus
Potential failure mode: ESD strike at J301 damages the transceiver
Potential effect: Permanent CAN failure and field return
Cause or mechanism: J301 pins are externally accessible on the vehicle harness. ESD current must be clamped before it can propagate into the board
Current controls: D301 PESD2CANFD27V rated at 20 kV IEC 61000-4-2 contact discharge and - corrected during this design review - RELOCATED to sit adjacent to J301 at x = 141.05 mm against the connector at 146.79 mm and ahead of L301 in the signal path per TCAN4550 datasheet section 11.1. The TCAN4550 also carries on-chip bus ESD protection
Recommended action: Perform IEC 61000-4-2 contact and air discharge testing at J301 to the target level; verify absence of latent damage by functional test after each strike series
Closure evidence: ESD test report recording levels strike counts and post-test functional results
Status: OPEN - layout mitigation applied and test outstanding

Design function: Keep the CAN transceiver within its operating junction temperature
Potential failure mode: Junction temperature exceeds the 125 degC operating limit or reaches the 160 degC thermal shutdown
Potential effect: Thermal shutdown and CAN dropout; accelerated ageing and reduced service life
Cause or mechanism: Dominant-state dissipation is estimated at about 0.45 W. With RthetaJA of 35.2 degC/W that gives roughly a 16 degC rise so Tj is about 101 degC at 85 degC ambient. U301 is the hottest device on the board. This is calculation only with no thermal measurement and a sustained bus fault raises the internal VCCOUT LDO dissipation further
Current controls: Six thermal vias under the U301 exposed pad into the In1 and B.Cu ground planes; VSUP fed from the 6.49 V rail rather than raw battery which minimises internal LDO drop
Recommended action: Thermal-image the board at maximum bus load and at 85 degC ambient including a sustained CANH/CANL short case; verify the Tj margin against the 125 degC limit
Closure evidence: Thermal imaging report recording ambient load and calculated junction temperature

Design function: Survive a reversed battery pigtail at the pack connector
Potential failure mode: Reverse voltage applied to the backup branch
Potential effect: Damage to U401 and U402; pack short circuit; potential thermal event on a lithium-ion cell
Cause or mechanism: J401 is a polarised JST PH connector but the pack pigtail can still be mis-wired during assembly or service
Current controls: U401 LM66100-Q1 configured for always-on reverse-current blocking with CE taken through R401 10 kohm to VOUT per datasheet section 8.3.2; R401 is the datasheet-recommended RCE which limits CE pin current to under 0.5 mA at -4.2 V; F401 1 A fuse; R402 2 ohm inrush limiter keeps the U401 body-diode pulse below its 2.5 A rating
Recommended action: Apply -4.2 V at J401 for 60 s and measure CE pin current and U401 case temperature; confirm no current flows into +3V0_BAT
Closure evidence: Reverse-insertion bench test record
Status: OPEN - design follows the datasheet but is not yet tested

Design function: Survive reverse connection of the vehicle harness
Potential failure mode: Reverse current path established into the buck or the downstream rails
Potential effect: Buck and LDO damage; at high fault current a board thermal event
Cause or mechanism: An installer reverses the two wires at J101. D102 is the only blocking element in the path
Current controls: D102 PNE20010ER-Q series rectifier blocks the reverse path; D101 is the bidirectional CA variant so it deliberately does NOT clamp a reverse connection which means the fuse is not forced open and the board simply sits inert; F101 remains in series
Recommended action: Bench-test -14 V and -36 V applied at J101 for 60 s; measure reverse leakage and the D102 junction temperature; confirm no downstream rail rises above zero
Closure evidence: Reverse-polarity test record including thermal measurement
Status: OPEN - design intent sound but untested

Design function: Provide a 50 ohm controlled-impedance antenna feed
Potential failure mode: Feed line impedance is not 50 ohm
Potential effect: Additional mismatch loss which compounds the RF-001 error and further reduces range
Cause or mechanism: RF traces are drawn at 0.18 mm and the RF netclass now declares the same width, so design intent and copper agree. The open question is the value itself, not the consistency. Calculated microstrip impedance on the 0.11 mm 2116 prepreg with er 4.29 and 35 um copper is about 55.6 ohm at 0.18 mm against about 52.3 ohm at 0.20 mm; roughly 0.215 mm is needed for 50 ohm. Fabricator etch tolerance is not accounted for
Current controls: Stackup is RF-appropriate with thin prepreg to a continuous In1 ground; controlled-impedance requirement and test coupon are specified in FAB_NOTES.md
Recommended action: Have the fabricator confirm the trace width required for 50 ohm plus or minus 10 percent on their actual stackup and adjust before tooling; require an impedance coupon and report with the shipment
Closure evidence: Fabricator impedance report from the production panel

Design function: Select vehicle or battery source without interrupting the MCU domain
Potential failure mode: Both ORing devices turn off simultaneously and +3V3_SYS collapses
Potential effect: Total loss of the MCU domain - the module is dead until one source is removed
Cause or mechanism: The LM66100-Q1 datasheet section 9.2.2 documents this corner explicitly: if both inputs sit at the same voltage for a long period both cross-coupled devices switch off. The CE comparator threshold is 80 mV
Current controls: DESIGNED OUT - the rails are deliberately offset by 300 mV with U102 at 3.3 V on the vehicle side and U402 at 3.0 V on the battery side which is well beyond the 80 mV comparator window. This is the specific reason U402 is a 3.0 V part rather than 3.3 V
Recommended action: Verify the offset holds across tolerance and temperature at both regulator extremes - 3.3 V at -2 percent gives 3.234 V against 3.0 V at +2 percent giving 3.06 V so 174 mV worst case which still exceeds 80 mV; bench-test a slow vehicle-rail decay to confirm clean handover
Closure evidence: Worst-case tolerance calculation plus a slow-ramp handover scope capture

Design function: Survive a CAN bus short to a vehicle rail or to ground
Potential failure mode: CANH or CANL shorts to 24 V 12 V or chassis ground
Potential effect: Transceiver damage and loss of communication for every node on the bus
Cause or mechanism: Harness chafing or connector mis-wiring. The bus is externally exposed at J301 and runs the length of the vehicle
Current controls: D301 PESD2CANFD27V has a 27 V standoff chosen specifically so that a short to a 24 V vehicle rail does not put the clamp into conduction; the TCAN4550 provides internal bus fault protection and thermal shutdown at 160 degC; the VCCOUT LDO current-limits during a fault
Recommended action: Bench-test CANH and CANL shorted to +24 V +12 V and GND individually and together for a sustained period; confirm automatic recovery and measure device temperature throughout
Closure evidence: Bus fault test record including recovery verification

Design function: Release a buildable bill of materials
Potential failure mode: X301 carries no manufacturer part number
Potential effect: Board cannot be quoted or built; an assembler substitution risks the wrong load capacitance or tolerance and therefore CAN timing failure
Cause or mechanism: The 40 MHz CAN reference crystal was never selected. Its frequency tolerance directly drives CAN FD bit timing and its motional parameters determine the final C303/C304 and R311 values which is why CAN-002 cannot close without it
Current controls: Value and load capacitance are recorded as 40 MHz CL 8 pF; candidate parts are listed in BOM_NOTES.md
Recommended action: Select an AEC-Q200 40 MHz CL 8 pF crystal; confirm its frequency tolerance against the TCAN4550 requirement; update and release the BOM
Closure evidence: Released BOM carrying the committed manufacturer part number

Design function: Build the intended assembly variant
Potential failure mode: DNP parts fitted when they should not be or omitted when they are required
Potential effect: Fitting C210/C211 on top of the internal cap array detunes the 48 MHz crystal; fitting termination on a stub node loads the bus; omitting it at an end node causes reflections
Cause or mechanism: Five DNP parts - C210 C211 C309 R302 R303 - whose correct state depends on the assembly variant and on the network topology
Current controls: DNP flags set in the schematic and carried into the BOM Fitted column; KiCad plots DNP parts crossed out on the fabrication layer; intent documented per item
Recommended action: Issue an explicit build-variant document naming the fitted or not-fitted state for each of the five parts; verify at first-article inspection
Closure evidence: Signed build variant sheet plus a first-article check record

Design function: Provide reliable SPI communication between the MCU and the CAN controller
Potential failure mode: Wrong SPI mode clock rate or bit order
Potential effect: Corrupted register reads and writes; intermittent or completely absent CAN traffic
Cause or mechanism: The TCAN4550 requires SPI mode 0 and supports up to 18 MHz while the CC2340R53 at 3.3 V should be limited to 12 MHz for its own timing. The bus runs on DIO18 DIO13 DIO12 and DIO11
Current controls: R301 10 kohm nCS pull-up keeps the device deselected while the MCU is in reset; R308 to R310 100 kohm define SCLK SDI and SDO levels when the MCU tri-states during backup; the requirement is noted on the schematic
Recommended action: Confirm SPI mode 0 and a clock of 12 MHz or below in firmware; scope setup and hold margins at the selected rate over the temperature range
Closure evidence: Scope captures of SPI timing at the selected clock rate

Design function: Allow firmware load and debug in manufacturing and service
Potential failure mode: SWD access unavailable or unreliable
Potential effect: Cannot program at end of line; cannot debug field returns
Cause or mechanism: J202 is a Tag-Connect TC2030 footprint - a spring-pin pad array with no fitted connector - so it depends on the correct probe and on good pad surface finish. SWO on pin 6 is left unconnected so trace output is unavailable
Current controls: TC2030 footprint with VCC SWDIO SWDCK RESET and GND all connected; RST_N additionally carries the R201 pull-up and C215
Recommended action: Verify programming with the actual TC2030 probe on a first article; confirm the HAL lead-free finish does not compromise spring-pin contact resistance; decide whether SWO is required and connect it if so
Closure evidence: Successful end-of-line programming demonstration on the first article

Design function: Keep the regulators within rating across the full input range
Potential failure mode: Excess dissipation in U101 or U102 at maximum input voltage
Potential effect: Reduced service life; thermal shutdown; rail collapse under combined high load and high ambient
Cause or mechanism: U102 drops 6.49 V to 3.3 V which at the roughly 20 mA design load is only about 64 mW - but that load has never been measured with the radio transmitting. U101 losses are estimated at about 70 mW at the assumed 110 mA output
Current controls: The key mitigation is architectural - U102 is fed from the 6.49 V intermediate rail rather than from VIN which cuts LDO dissipation by roughly ten times; both regulators use PowerPAD packages with 10 and 6 thermal vias respectively
Recommended action: Measure actual rail currents with BLE transmitting and CAN at full bus load; recompute dissipation against the measured rather than the estimated load
Closure evidence: Rail current measurement table taken under worst-case activity
